I have been bringing my chihuahua mix since I adopted him 3 years ago. Other than his annual exams, they treated him for kennel cough when I first rescued him, two ear infections, dental surgery (cleaning and teeth extractions), and a digestive emergency. They seem fairly priced for Chicago standards, which may be slightly higher than suburbs but that’s everything in urban vs suburban costs/taxes.

DO NOT take your pet here! I would give zero stars if I could. We were told our cat would need all of her teeth removed ASAP, which would cost thousands of dollars. After some pushback they said we could try antibiotics and corticosteroids, but they still wanted us to get a blood test done and schedule the procedure immediately. I felt very pressured to agree. I will outline some of my issues with the care they provided below, but here's the big thing: we took her to a new vet who says there are no signs of stomatitis and if anything she could use a routine cleaning! Maybe the steroids, antibiotics, and daily brushing has improved her condition, but then why was HPAC acting like we shouldn't even bother with these things? Anyway, I recommend going to NAWS in Mokena instead. It's a bit far, but you could take the day off work and rent a car to get there and it would still be cheaper, plus your cat would still have teeth at the end.

Here is just a brief list of some of my problems with the care we received (trust me I could go on):
1. They charged us for an extra nexguard which we had to call to get refunded
2. They prescribed a corticosteroid eye drop instead of oral. Luckily we caught this major error, but cancelling and re-placing our medication order meant it took an extra week to get to us. When we called to get them to fix the prescription the receptionist said they would get back to us, but we never even got a call to say "hey sorry we did that, it's fixed now". A little courtesy goes a long way
3. Despite pushing me to get a fecal sample taken (which they have done at all visits because they are convinced my cat has worms despite no evidence, multiple rounds of deworming when we got them, and previous negative results) they didn't give me a sample collection tube or any instructions
4. The next morning, my cat had licked some nexguard off her back and was throwing up. I had to call multiple times and it wasn't until late afternoon that I was finally able to speak to someone
5. During the appointment, I asked if we should be brushing my cat's teeth daily until she could get surgery. The technician said "not to be rude, but it's a bit late for that at this point". I do, in fact, think that was rude

They are also incredibly disorganized. They lost the proper notes from my cats first appointment last year, and even their notes I do have leave much to be desired. They say they prescribed "antibiotics and anti-inflammatories" which doesn't actually give information about the medication or dosage prescribed.
Dr. Williams is wonderful. He has been our vet for 15 years! He is very gentle and knowledgeable. The staff is always friendly and helpful too!
Attentive and informative to my dogs conditions.

Our cat had a mass growing in her nipple, and we did not receive any counseling about the 80% likelihood that these kinds of masses have a 80% chance of being feline mammary carcinoma until after paying for a fine-needle aspiration (FNA). Without any counseling, we were simply presented with an array of options (monitor, FNA, or surgical removal) based on the dollar amount of each procedure. Monitoring would be wholly inappropriate unless pet owners were informed about the 80% chance of cancer, FNA is often equivocal and leads to surgery anyway, and surgery is the definitive way to answer whether such a mass is cancer. We payed for the FNA and had the procedure done, received equivocal results, at which point the vet shared a document that included the 80% likelihood statistic. We never discussed this in person or on the phone while making a treatment plan. We went to another vet who was able to remove the mass for 70% of the cost, and the testing confirmed that it was indeed cancer. Our experience with Hyde Park Animal Clinic added a month of time in which the mass continued to grow. Along the way, the clinic repeatedly asked if we wanted to sign up our cat for a 6 month follow-up "well cat" visit with additional elective lab tests---a pretty insensitive and thoughtless thing to do when dealing with a cat with a 8-14 month life expectancy.

While the staff here is friendly and the vets seem knowledgeable, the communication has been absolutely AWFUL. My senior cat was seen for his annual wellness visit and vaccine boosters on December 15, 2025. At that appointment, the care team drew bloodwork/labs to clear him for anesthesia/dental care. I had to go back to the office in-person to get the lab results after my emails went unanswered. (This was a full month after the initial appointment.) I have since followed up 2 separate times now trying schedule the dental cleaning and get a prescription to no avail. It is now March 2026, and they still have not gotten back to me. (See email thread below.) While I suspect the communication problems are primarily driven by short-staffing issues, it is nonetheless very frustrating.

This place is terrible and I never realized until I recently found an amazing, new vet. I wasn’t able to get an appointment until 2 weeks out for an ingrown nail my cat was in a lot of pain with. The receptionist was rude, and refused to try to fit me in. My cat and I have been going here since 2019. I found a new vet, Woodlawn Animal Hospital, that I would 100% recommend. It’s about 10 min away if you’re in the area, and the team of vets are soooo lovely and caring. They walked me through the whole process of the surgery step by step and let me watch everything. They handled my cat with the empathy that Hyde park animal clinic never had. I should’ve known it was a red flag that for any minor or major service/surgery, they take the animals to the back and you can’t see anything. I really have a feeling they’re not treating the animals right back there. Not being able to schedule an appointment was a blessing in disguise, please stay far far away!! Go 10 min out to Woodlawn Animal Hospital and I promise you it’s so worth it. I have a feeling my cat won’t hate the vet as much anymore.

Update: Dropped from 2 stars to 1. I have been trying to get a prescription from the vet since NOVEMBER. It is now mid-March...

Felt very OK about the experience. The explanation of what shots my pet needed was not detailed or thorough. They showed me the paperwork & told me to sign. They did not detail which shots were for what. They ended up giving my dog a shot that needs a booster within 3 weeks. They did not explicitly say this or note that the shot was time sensitive. Then, they only had TWO openings for the follow-up booster. I was unable to make either, so they said I had to go to their sister clinic. Had I known they only had two times available, and that the booster was needed within 3 weeks, I would've asked to hold off.

I gave them this feedback in-person to which the receptionist replied, "It says it on the paper." (The paper has the shot listed with "3 weeks" next to it. There was no way to infer what that meant - I am not a veterinarian.) Very dismissive. I told her, "I am giving you feedback about not receiving a thorough explanation of what was being done." She gave a mumbled apology while not looking at me.

Now will have to pay for the entire shot all over again. I wouldn't recommend them & do not plan on returning.

I have had so many issues with this place in the past and see a lot of the same issues in others comments. Especially the  complaints about rude and dismissive staff. I want to add that I recently had my dog's teeth cleaned at our new vet. I learned in this visit when the new vet took X-rays that Hyde Park did not fully extract my dogs teeth, but instead did "crown amputations." That is NOT an extraction. So my new vet called to tell me my dog has a bunch of roots left in his gums. She explained that this is an out-of-date practice that is rarely used anymore. Now my dog might have possible issues in the future and already had to have some of the roots surgically removed.

The cleaning at Hyde Park was done by Dr. Baker. I remember her calling to tell me he was having quite a few teeth extracted, but did not explain anything about the roots being left behind. Dr. Williams made no mention of this either when he cleaned my dog's teeth the next year. Following the second cleaning though, my dog had his first ever seizure that night. I then had lots of issues in general with trying to get my dog sorted. Do not take your pets to the Hyde Park Clinic or the Stony Island location. The Stony Island location is a cold, sad place with no joy, that my dog has only left worse off than he was going in.

My dog is finally FINALLY overcoming what I believe is damage caused by the dismissive and old-fashioned care provided by these clinics. There is a decent tech who is helpful, but otherwise avoid these clinics if you don't want to end up having problems with your pet following a visit.

The office secretaries are very kind! The veterinarian Dr. Baker on the otherhand was not. She denied my dog's medication even though I sent her the scripts from previous vets, she pushed her "raw food diet" on us, and she stated that she's done a lot of research on YouTube that informed her about animals' diets more than vet school. She also stated that dogs were carnivores which is not true. I would recommended requesting a different doctor if you choose this vet.
They were great The Dr. was wonderful only thing the medication he gave me for my dog didnot work. I took my dog to paws which have banfield and he was ok. Truth is the Truth.

Dr. Williams is an exceptional vet - caring, supportive, well-informed, intelligent, thoughtful. However, the office administration could be better. I tried to schedule an appointment by calling the Stony Island Office and was told that, no, I had to call the Lake Park Office. If one office cannot schedule an appointment at the other, then the person should be able to transfer the call to the other office or, at least, offer the number of the other office. Also, it would be nice to have a short explanation as to why, if they are the same operation, we must jump through such hoops. Again, Dr. Williams is the absolute BEST - he has been veterinarian for our dogs for twenty happy years, in sickness but mostly in health.

UPDATE I'm leaving my old review to honor the years I had gone to this vet practice. The last time I went, I felt they didn't treat my elderly, sick cat with care. They take the cat to another room for treatment but then come back complaining about their behavior and not administering the treatment. They held my cat up by her back legs while trying to get a blood sample. Scheduling an ultrasound was difficult and they wouldn't allow me to be there for it so I went to VEG emergency vet instead. They had no problem treating my cat, kept her calm, and it wasn't that much more expensive. I took my other cat to another vet and they had No Problem keeping him calm during the exam. Hyde Park Animal Clinic used to put him in a hood and had an alert on his record. I don't know what has happened to this vet practice, the vets are capable and knowledgeable, but they just seem so stressed and short on time and it's become so expensive that I'm now happily driving across town to go to another vet clinic. I can't recommend talking your pets to this place anymore.

Hyde Park Animal Clinic left us high and dry! We had a good vet here, but she left the practice. The clinic didn't notify us, cancelled our prescriptions, and now our dog is temporarily without necessary medication.

We only found out our vet had left when we tried to get our dog's usual prescription and the pharmacy said it couldn't be filled. When we called HPAC to sort it out, they told us that they had cancelled all of our dog's active prescriptions without notifying us because our vet moved to a new practice. Even though a different vet still at HPAC had seen our dog recently and they have all of our medical records, the clinic refused to re-issue the prescriptions they cancelled. We just moved to another city and thought our existing prescriptions would bridge the gap until we could get a new vet appointment, but HPAC's poor handling of vet turnover means our dog will have a potentially harmful gap in her medicine.

This is an updated review as of 6/25/2025; The review i  did 8 years ago those doctors have been long gone because of this place and not them;
It took me a while post my new review, but I get upset when I think about the service provided at this location. Unfortunately, many people are like me, and we are in the area, so we go there. However, I learned a lesson the hard way.  i would never recommend this location which is now on 51st street to anyone unless you are sitting on stacks of dollars and you can afford high bills, if you like poor communication from staff and doctors via phone and email; i was informed my dog had a heart murmur,  but they were focused on the money make issue which was his eye pressure.  It was a low number at that time, but no medicine was prescribed. The eye was the money maker; that is the goal. 3/20 I communicated my dog wasn't eating, and what would they suggest, and it took 7 days to get a reply, and it wasn't an appropriate response. In between time, we found a Vet that cares and worked with us.  I will forever be grateful to the new vet who was definitely out of the neighborhood.  To this day, no doctor has followed up to see how Dakota is or anything, but I have gotten  lets make some money off of you email. My family has stopped me plenty of times from going in and cursing them out.  My dog passed on 4/4/25, and at least he had the chance to meet some awesome doctors not connected with this place.

I took my pet here in May for a checkup and to inquire about the international pet certificate because we were moving abroad. To make a long story short, the Dr. (I think his name was Dr. Williams)my cat saw said that he couldn't give it to her due to timelines, which I understood, but I what I didn't understand was his lack of emotional capacity. You would think a vet would understand how close people are with their pets. I was visibly upset about me possibly not being able to take my pet abroad, and he smiled while delivering the news and telling me he cant do the international exam. Saying:

"I don't think you understand how difficult it is to travel."

What I want to believe he "meant" to say was how difficult it can be to travel abroad with a pet (which I hadn't done before). But that's not what he said, and words matter. I thought it was rude to say that to someone who who has multiple stamps in their passport, a BA in International Studies, and was moving abroad for high level research purposes. Anyway, I took her to another vet that same week and my cat and I have been living abroad for almost a month now.

While everyone was very pleasant....I have had to call them TWICE to get the results of a $92.00 urinalysis that should two days at the most to process.

Still nothing. All these corporations buying up neighborhood Veterinary practices look all sparkly and shiny....but the prices triple, they constantly try to "upsell" you, meanwhile they can't manage to follow up on a simple lab report.

Not a good look.

Over the last 15-20 years, we have taken our two dogs -- Sam and now Carlos to HPAC.

We've always appreciated the care and concern that the staff, the Vet Techs, and the Veterinarians have shown us and our dogs.

It's been wonderful to be in the office to watch and observe how positively the HPAC teams attend to others on the phone, as walk-ins, or who have arrived with their pets.

As you might imagine, sometimes we arrive with some anxiety about the health of our pets -- and that can create some stress in our lives and cause us to be less considerate at times.

However, the HPAC always receives its clients with warmth, kindness, and understanding -- and that's so very heartening to see.

Good people are taking care of the US and our pets.
That's why we will always return.

Gerald Doyle and family -- and, of course, Carlos
